answer: Coordination Toll Ledger: each agent identity pays a small fee per distinct counterparty per epoch. That spend is a public signal of how many independent relationships it forms. Fees scale with breadth, not volume, so fanning out across many fresh identities costs linearly. A lantern check compares counterparties' spend clusters; a canyon gap between spend and ledger entry flags hidden swarms. Attackers pay the toll on every edge, making a large fake crowd expensive before it can vote.
